title: Learning and Verifying Stabilizing Controllers with Structured Neural Control Lyapunov Functions
abstract: arXiv:2611.21009v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This work investigates the joint learning of neural controllers and control Lyapunov functions (CLFs) for nonlinear discrete-time systems. We exploit the structural properties of Input Convex Neural Networks and Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Networks to guarantee positive definiteness of CLF candidates by construction, reducing the conditions requiring formal verification. We develop a mixed-integer programming framework to formally verify the remaining stability conditions and introduce an iterative region of attraction (ROA) expansion procedure to enlarge the certified ROA without retraining. Experiments on an inverted pendulum and a path-tracking system demonstrate the advantages of structured neural CLFs, particularly PLNets, and illustrate how their structural bounds influence the geometry of the certified regions. Our code is available at: https://github.com/JLedesMart/Structured-Neural-Control-Lyapunov-Functions.

translated_title: 基于结构化神经控制李雅普诺夫函数的稳定控制器学习与验证
translated_abstract: 本研究针对非线性离散时间系统，探索了神经控制器与控制李雅普诺夫函数（CLF）的联合学习。我们利用输入凸神经网络和Polyak-Łojasiewicz网络的结构特性，通过构造方式保证CLF候选函数的正定性，从而减少了需要形式化验证的条件。我们开发了一个混合整数规划框架来形式化验证剩余的稳定性条件，并引入了一种迭代式的吸引域（ROA）扩展方法，无需重新训练即可扩大经认证的吸引域。在倒立摆和路径跟踪系统上的实验展示了结构化神经CLF（特别是PLNets）的优势，并说明了其结构界如何影响认证区域的几何形状。我们的代码已开源于：https://github.com/JLedesMart/Structured-Neural-Control-Lyapunov-Functions。
tldr: 本文利用输入凸神经网络与Polyak-Łojasiewicz网络的结构特性，在构造层面保证控制李雅普诺夫函数的正定性，并结合混合整数规划形式化验证与迭代吸引域扩展方法，实现了非线性离散时间系统中稳定控制器与CLF的联合学习与认证。
en_tdlr: This work jointly learns neural controllers and control Lyapunov functions for nonlinear discrete-time systems by exploiting the structural properties of Input Convex Neural Networks and PLNets to guarantee positive definiteness by construction, while formally verifying stability conditions via mixed-integer programming and enlarging the certified region of attraction through an iterative expansion procedure without retraining.
